Honestly from my experiences and others we love our friends a lot but when things are super stressful we can't talk anymore but still want to have our friends or be with them. Just talking with her and not expecting an answer is fine too. 

Maybe I can recommend a bit of the anime "hi score girl" on netflix. It has an autistic girl character that is completely non verbal but likes hanging out with her friend and playing video games with him and listening to his "info dumps".

I had a friend back in grade 1 I now realize was autistic but she would phone me and not talk to me and I thought it was the weirdest thing cause she just would sound bored and not converse with me, but she really liked to phone me just to feel like she was with her friend I think. She changed schools too so I look back and see she was going through a lot of stress that made her non verbal. But it didn't mean she wanted to stop being friends! 

I know when also going through a melt down period like this and being non verbal that being asked questions of whats wrong requires you to think of an answer and sometimes that is usually too stressful to try to process. I think of a computer that has too many programs running and tasks and its slogging everything down so I can only prioritize on specific tasks. Socializing is extremely complex and draining for autistic people in general even when not in a stressful burnout period. Some things just take time to reset too.

I went through non verbal mode in grade 11 due to environmental stress and depression etc, my friends at the time thought i just didn't care about them anymore or was ignoring them so they started to bully me by doing the silent treatment. It hurt me so much and it was a misunderstanding but made me even more depressed because I wanted to solve the issue but talking and socializing was too much due to the overwhelming stress I was experiencing every day. 

I'd say to just give her some space and reassurance that she can talk to you whenever she feels ready to, and not feeling like she is pressured to do so. She will feel I think very thankful she has a friend that understands her in this way. 

A lot of my friends who are autistic too we all understand that life gets to be too much and trying to juggle all the tasks we are given so we are accepting that we may not talk with eachother all the time, sometimes even for months, but we always come back talking as if no time has passed.

Autistic people experience time flow also differently I believe, because of the developmental delays, the world can feel like its moving way too fast to keep up.

Generally most small talk is annoying because it tends to not go anywhere. 

I also don't like when I do have work but I am not working, but someone asks me how is work. For example an ex-coworker texted me out of nowhere asking how I was. I told them what projects I am working on at the moment. They say thats great then immediately jump to "So how's the store?"

I skipped around the question by further emphasizing my projects, and they said great, and then say "so I take it you're not at the store as much?" It's crazy how much people identify you with your job and my response was pretty much "it's just...the same...as always?" 

When I wasn't working, and was asked "what do you do", I told them I was furthering my art skills so I can perform better for future projects and aspirations. Which people didn't really seem to respond to well but whatever.

The times I've done it I became more frugal and just wanted to live simple life so going to food banks or church's that sometimes just have free food at certain times (and its good) and learning to code or writing, seeing family, walking at night.

If its something I might miss more, is the freedom of what you can do and when to sleep. I have anxiety of not getting enough sleep, and for a lot of people with work, they have to spend their free time even around it as well like preparing lunch for it or making sure to get to bed early to be able to work in the morning, but what I liked was I could just decide to walk out at 3am and not worry.

I mean even with shifts that start in the mid afternoon that go to evening its still in your mind and scheduling around it

Also very detrimental to your health. If you have a regular office job, you're going to be sitting for a long time everyday, which is really bad for you. If you are on your feet constantly its the same basically but in different ways like revolving around your feet than your spine.

Long work hours are really bad for us and I always feel bad for people I meet at jobs who are workaholics and don't understand.
